body: Given my previous experience with overcoming adblockers - resulting html (class name, id, title, url etc) of the area (not necessary element itself) should not contain anything that could be treated as a description of an advertisement, like: banner, ad, ads etc.
So I think the content needs to be reworked to be something not ad related. Perhaps it could be an upcoming hero events component?
@StephenFluin - I have moved this to the docs project and relabelled as it is not related to the AIO doc-viewer but instead content related.
I confirm that any js or image with "ad" in its name is likely to be blocked by adblocks, I've had this issue before
If you looking for an  alternative example, refer this **[medium](https://medium.com/@aravind_12433/load-modal-component-dynamically-in-angular-5fda8e1dc3e7)** post

body:
@jenniferfell I was able to reproduce this. Make sure you have 'EasyList' selected in AdBlock, that's the one that is doing it for me.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/165056/39247387-2429401a-484e-11e8-9163-97e475fc6576.png)

I am able to reproduce this as well (Chrome 70.0.3538.102 with Adblock Plus). The culprit seems to be in the `ad-banner` class in ad-banner.component.ts. Like @StephenFluin mentioned, this is due to EasyList being selected in ABP. It injects `display:none` in elements with the `ad-banner` class name.

An easy fix for this is to just rename the `ad-banner` class to `ad-banner-example`, after which the banner works as expected.
